chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'For every divorced woman is a provision (mut'ah), except for the woman who divorces by al-khul', for she has bought herself.'

key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةَ: The woman who divorces by khul' (buying herself out)
key_terms.مُتْعَةٌ: Provision or parting gift given to the wife upon divorce

ai.seo_question: Who is exempt from the divorce provision (mut'ah) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of al-Kulayni, clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between standard divorce and khul' by attributing the ruling to Imam Ali (AS). It establishes that the financial gift (mut'ah) is a right for most divorced women, whereas the khul' woman is excluded because she effectively 'purchased' her release from the marital bond, a principle rooted in the Prophet's tradition. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the contractual nature of khul' where the wife's initiative to dissolve the marriage alters her financial entitlements.
